questions.fullText: Passage: A galvanometer is an instrument used to show the direction and strength of the current passing through it. It essentially works on the fact that a current-carrying coil experiences a deflecting torque when placed in a magnetic field. A spring attached to the coil provides a counter torque. In equilibrium, the deflecting torque is balanced by the restoring torque of the spring: NBAI = kφ. A small resistance, called a shunt, of a suitable value is connected in parallel with the galvanometer.
